newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Trading in Ceylon Oxygen suspended.
newsitem.headline: Trading in Ceylon Oxygen suspended.

text.p: The Colombo Stock Exchange said on Wednesday it had suspended trading in Ceylon Oxygen Ltd which announced a rights issue at a premium to the current market price.
The company offered a one-for-two rights at 60 rupees a share against its last traded price of 47.50 rupees.

"Stock Exchange rules do not prevent a company from pricing rights at a premium. But since it is the first time this has been done, the information has to be fully disseminated," an exchange official told Reuters.
The company defended the pricing by saying that current low market price had nothing to do with the company's performance but only reflected depressed market conditions.
Ceylon Oxygen, which is the monopoly manufacturer of industrial and medical gases in Sri Lanka, is a subsidiary of Norway's Norsk Hydro AS.
